content:
Longtime Democratic strategist James Carville has heaped scorn on his party’s new rules for 2028 presidential hopefuls, arguing that its effort to curb the influence of dark money and outside spending in the primaries could backfire.

The Democratic National Committee is requiring prospective candidates to sign a pledge denouncing their involvement with super PACs or dark money groups to qualify for DNC-sanctioned debates. See the pledge here.

Carville was less than impressed, slamming the move on the latest episode of his “Politics War Room” podcast, released Wednesday.

“First of all, that’s not your fucking job, alright?” he said, suggesting that funding should be debated on the stage among the candidates themselves.

“I don’t know where the DNC gets off making a policy requirement for somebody to get in the debate, but, I’m not even sure this is good policy,” he continued. “Because I tell you, the group of people in the country that are in politics that most wanna see this policy? Well, the billionaire class.”

Carville pointed to billionaire Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, a potential 2028 Democratic contender, who he described as “a great guy,” to illustrate his argument.

“JB Pritzker don’t give a shit. He don’t need Super PAC funding,” said the strategist.

“What they do is, they get in a meeting and they wanna ‘stand up to the billionaire class,’ when, in fact, you’re helping the fucking billionaire class,” he added.

Carville then sent a blunt message to party officials:

“Let me tell the DNC members something. You know who runs this party? The people who vote in our primaries. Maximize their influence and diminish your influence, and we’ll be successful.”
